split_method: chronological; candidates compared only on 2024 data (rolling folds for demand, Oct-Dec 2024 for shortage), final models refitted on all of 2024 and tested once on 2025

demand.kpi: Predicted units requested during the next seven days

selection.candidate: Benchmark: 7-day arrival forecast × units per arrival (no fitting)
Gradient boosting with item code (first Week 10 version)
Gradient boosting with arrival-driven expected demand
Linear regression on expected and recent demand

demand.selection_rule: lowest mean WAPE over four rolling 2024 validation folds; candidates within 0.25 percentage points are treated as tied and the first-listed (simplest, no item code) design is preferred

shortage.kpi: Probability of any backorder during the next seven days
shortage.algorithm: Logistic regression on coverage and trend predictors, class-weighted, with sigmoid probability calibration

selection.candidate: Logistic regression on coverage and trend predictors

shortage.selection_rule: highest validation average precision (suited to rare outcomes)
shortage.threshold_rule: maximum F1 on the Oct-Dec 2024 validation period

interpretation_method: Overall importance uses test-set permutation importance on the raw predictors. Individual contributions use one-predictor-at-a-time replacement with the training reference value; contributions are predictive, approximate, may not sum exactly because of interactions, and are not causal effects.
limitations: All observations and outcomes are synthetic.
Only eight consumables from one simulated emergency department are represented.
Shortages are rare (24 positive test rows), so precision is low and probabilities need recalibration on real data.
Scenario changes are model-based comparisons, not guaranteed intervention effects.
